page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz on the ARMv8 architecture, with 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the t2a-standard-2 is positioned for entry-level or lightweight workloads. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the average range. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks show limitations. The Geekbench multi-core score, Passmark CPU score, and memory bandwidth tests fall into the weak to poor categories. For instance, the uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is 26.99 GB/sec, and the Passmark memory score is in the bottom 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also register in the weak category, with Redis achieving 2.61 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-2 offers a low-cost entry point into ARM64 cloud computing, leveraging the power-efficient Ampere architecture to deliver dedicated resources without the premium of traditional x86 architectures. Given its resource profile and benchmark results, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, including basic web serving, software development and compilation testing for ARM64, microservices, and low-traffic database operations.
